title: TradingView Basics
hook: Your chart is your workspace. Learn it before you try to read it.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to set up a clean, readable chart instead of a cluttered one.

blocks.heading: TradingView is your workspace, not just a pretty chart

beats.heading: Read, zoom, mark
beats.body: You're using it to read price, change perspective with timeframes, and mark behavior so your eyes stop feeling lost.

beats.heading: A few tools, used clearly
beats.body: A horizontal level marking a repeated reaction area is one of the cleanest beginner tools — you don't need every feature.

blocks.heading: What did she get wrong?
blocks.scenario: A new trader adds ten different drawing tools to her chart at once, hoping more markings will make her read clearer.

options.label: An overloaded chart makes price harder to read, not easier
options.feedback: Right — clutter competes with price for your attention.

options.label: Nothing — more tools always means a better read
options.feedback: More markings isn't automatically more useful information.

blocks.quote: You do not need every feature. A few tools used clearly is better than a messy chart.

questions.question: Does adding more drawing tools to a chart automatically make analysis more accurate?
options: No — a cluttered chart makes it harder to see what price is actually doing
Yes — more tools always means more accuracy
Only if the tools are different colors
questions.why: A few clearly-used tools usually beat a chart covered in every available drawing tool.

questions.question: Switching timeframes changes your ___ on the same market, not the market itself.
questions.why: Zooming in or out just changes what detail you can see, not the underlying price story.

takeaways: TradingView is a workspace for reading price, not a decoration contest.
A cluttered chart makes price harder to read, not easier.
Switching timeframes changes your view — not the market itself.
remember: A few tools used clearly beats a messy chart.
